stories.author: cstadler1869
stories.title: Usenet rewind archive search engine
stories.groq_label: Usenet Rewind provides a functional search engine for historical Usenet archives as Google Groups degrades, while reviving privacy concerns over permanently public decades-old personal data.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Short:

This project addresses the difficulty of searching historical Usenet posts reliably without relying on Google Groups. Hacker News commenters generally appreciated its fast search capabilities and independent archiving and believed the project could make retro computing history and old Usenet posts easily accessible again. However, they also expressed concerns about permanent privacy exposure of old posts and questioned the lack of options to remove personal information posted decades ago. Overall, the discussion was mixed, with commenters recognizing both the project's potential and its limitations.

stories.author: rvz
stories.title: Navier-Stokes Announcement
stories.groq_label: The Clay Mathematics Institute acknowledged a claimed solution to the Navier-Stokes problem without naming OpenAI, adhering to rules that require two years of peer-reviewed publication before prize eligibility.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: Balanced

This announcement aims to solve the problem of evaluating claimed solutions to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem. The Hacker News discussion was generally mixed, with many commenters appreciating the institute's neutral statement and the project's approach to handling public drama without taking sides. At the same time, several commenters raised concerns about eligibility rules and philosophical implications, arguing that publishing outside peer-reviewed journals delays official recognition and that proving theorems without comprehension threatens mathematical work. Overall, the discussion suggests that the community sees promise in the project but believes there are important challenges that still need to be addressed.

stories.author: 1e1a
stories.title: google.com/goto: Google's anti-scraping update
stories.groq_label: Google search results now use base64-encoded protobuf redirect URLs to prevent scraping and obscure direct links.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: Executive Summary

This article attempts to solve automated search engine scraping and index abuse. Community feedback was largely centered around Google replacing direct search result URLs with obfuscated redirect links. Positive comments emphasized Google's legitimate need to protect its search index from unauthorized scraping and abuse, while negative comments focused on added redirect latency, increased user tracking, obfuscations that harm web openness, and the reality that well-funded scrapers will still bypass the restrictions. Although opinions differed on whether the change significantly harms everyday end users, the overall discussion indicates that the project is considered a frustrating anti-scraping measure, with both clear defensive capabilities and notable usability limitations.
